tables.name: users
tables.purpose: Stores user account information for the task manager application

columns.name: created_at
columns.notes: Timestamp when user account was created

columns.name: updated_at
columns.notes: Timestamp when user account was last updated

tables.name: tasks
tables.purpose: Stores task information including title, description, and completion status

columns.name: user_id
columns.notes: Foreign key referencing the user who owns this task

columns.name: is_completed
columns.notes: Flag indicating whether the task is completed

columns.name: completed_at
columns.notes: Timestamp when the task was marked as completed

columns.name: updated_at
columns.notes: Timestamp when task was last updated

relationships.notes: Each task belongs to one user

assumptions: User authentication and authorization will be handled at the application layer
Each task belongs to exactly one user (no task sharing between users)
Soft delete is not required; tasks are permanently deleted when removed
Task filtering by status (active/completed) will be handled via the is_completed boolean flag
UUID is used for primary keys to ensure global uniqueness and better security
Timestamps are automatically managed for audit trail purposes
Email and username are both unique to prevent duplicate accounts
Password storage uses hashing (implementation details handled by application layer)
Task title is mandatory while description is optional based on acceptance criteria
Completed tasks track completion timestamp for historical tracking
No task priority, due dates, or categories are required based on current feature set
No task assignment or collaboration features are needed (single user role)
